Twelve comments

Irene Meldrum’s Welcome To Bon Accord

This tune was composed by Bert Murray from Aberdeen and it is a 2/4 march originally.
I like the version from Lau a lot, so the notation sticks to this version of the tune.
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zSXHAXgumPk&list=PLTFN1-PvwPD1vDPvUvu82Ns6SmhVLbo2u&index=28

↳ Posted by Martin fiddle on February 8th, 2014.

Not Bert Murray.

This tune appears in Book 3 of the Cowal collection, and is attributed to William G Meldrum.
The book was published around 1920 when Bert was 7 years old. I met Bert a few times, and I don’t think he was one for “pinching” tunes.

↳ Posted by Weejie on February 8th, 2014.

Here is the (skeleton) setting from the Cowal Collection. It needs the gracing to give it “percussion”, so is pretty tame.
I’ll get round to submitting a fiddle version with the “snaps” in appropriate places in the not too distant future.

With fourth part, and going back to the first part

Weejie’s setting was missing the fourth part of the tune (which is over the page in the Cowal Collection), so I’ve added that in.

I’ve also added a version that repeats the “refrain” of the first part at the end of the other three parts, based on Tim Edey and Brendan Power’s recording on “Wriggle and Writhe”.

It’s attributed to William G Meldrum “Piper to The MacKintosh”, and son of Robert, in more than one source.

↳ Posted by Weejie on January 16th, 2015.

Re: Irene Meldrum’s Welcome To Bon Accord

kind of nice to think he might have written it for his daughter, who was born in 1911.

↳ Posted by David Bruce White on November 26th, 2020.

Re: Irene Meldrum’s Welcome To Bon Accord

I don’t know for sure who wrote it, but Irene was William Meldrum’s daughter’s name; she was born in 1911 and they lived in Union Grove, Aberdeen. The city’s motto is Bon Accord, said to date back to the massacre of the English garrison in Aberdeen Castle in 1308 led by Robert the Bruce. So I’m kind of hoping it was written about my mother…

↳ Posted by David Bruce White on December 13th, 2020.

Re: Irene Meldrum’s Welcome To Bon Accord

As it says above, David, there’s little doubt that it was composed by your grandfather, and it’s extremely likely that he wrote it for your mother.

↳ Posted by Nigel Gatherer on December 13th, 2020.

Re: Irene Meldrum’s Welcome To Bon Accord

The X:1 version is very confusing. The initial notes a-g in the first bar should, I think, be considered as a lead-in / anacrusis. As written, the tune shows the bar lines in the wrong places, meaning that it does not convey the stress properly. The actual first note of bar one should be the f#. It would be good if the contributor could edit this version. The subsequent versions give a far clearer impression of how the tune should be phrased.
